definitions.gloss: to make a mistake in writing; to write incorrectly; to botch writing
definitions.explanation: To fail at writing something correctly, resulting in an error. Often used for handwritten documents, addressing envelopes, or calligraphy. The ～損じる pattern means 'to fail at doing ~'.

examples.japanese: {宛名|あてな}を{書|か}き{損|そん}じた。
examples.english: I made a mistake writing the address.

examples.japanese: {年賀状|ねんがじょう}を{書|か}き{損|そん}じて、{新|あたら}しいはがきに{書|か}き{直|なお}した。
examples.english: I messed up the New Year's card and rewrote it on a new postcard.

examples.japanese: {書|か}き{損|そん}じたはがきは{郵便局|ゆうびんきょく}で{交換|こうかん}してもらえる。
examples.english: Postcards with writing mistakes can be exchanged at the post office.

notes:
COMMON PATTERNS:
Ichidan verb. The ～{損|そん}じる pattern attaches to the masu-stem of another verb to mean "to fail at doing ~." This is a slightly more formal variant of ～{損|そこ}なう.
- {読|よ}み{損|そん}じる (to misread)
- {言|い}い{損|そん}じる (to misspeak)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {書|か}き{損|そん}じたはがき (a postcard with a writing mistake)
- {書|か}き{損|そん}じを{直|なお}す (to correct a writing error)

USAGE:
{書|か}き{損|そん}じ (noun form) is commonly used to refer to a spoiled piece of writing, especially postcards. Japan Post offers exchanges for {書|か}き{損|そん}じはがき (spoiled postcards) for a small fee.
